claims.text: Solidified equiatomic FeNiCrMn is a single-phase FCC alloy.
The proposed initial alloy composition is Fe25Ni25Cr25Mn25.
The specified processing route produces an average grain size of approximately 20 µm.
The processed material is free of pre-existing twins and precipitates.
Temperature- and strain-rate-dependent activation of deformation twinning is the dominant mechanism controlling dynamic strength and ductility in solidified equiatomic FeNiCrMn.
Equiatomic FeNiCrMn has a medium stacking-fault energy of approximately 20 mJ m^-2.
At temperatures at or below 0 °C and strain rates at or above 10^3 s^-1, deformation twinning becomes significant.
Twin boundaries generated during deformation impede dislocation motion.
The increased twin-boundary density elevates work-hardening and maintains ductility.
At temperatures at or above 400 °C, plasticity occurs primarily by dislocation slip with minimal twinning.
At low strain rates at or below 10^-3 s^-1, plasticity occurs primarily by dislocation slip with minimal twinning.
At high temperature or low strain rate, increased cross-slip and climb suppress twinning.
Suppression of twinning at high temperature or low strain rate reduces hardening and ductility.
Relative to the 25 °C and 10^-3 s^-1 baseline, yield strength and work-hardening rate will increase by approximately 20–30% at temperatures at or below 0 °C and strain rates at or above 10^3 s^-1.
Twin volume fraction will exceed approximately 15% at temperatures at or below 0 °C and strain rates at or above 10^3 s^-1.
Twin volume fraction will be below approximately 5% at temperatures at or above 400 °C or strain rates at or below 10^-3 s^-1.
The proposed quasi-static compression baseline has a yield strength of approximately 400 MPa.
The proposed quasi-static compression baseline has approximately 50% total elongation.
The proposed quasi-static baseline has a twin fraction of approximately 5%.
Failure of strength and ductility variations to correlate with twin fraction would falsify the proposed twinning-controlled mechanism.

contradictions.description: The low-rate prediction applies to strain rates at or below 10^-3 s^-1 and says twin fraction falls below approximately 5%, while the baseline at exactly 10^-3 s^-1 specifies a twin fraction of approximately 5%. The use of an inclusive threshold makes these statements slightly inconsistent.
